source_text: Οὐ κτίσμα προσκυνοῦμεν· μὴ γένοιτο! Ἐθνικῶν γὰρ καὶ Ἀρειανῶν ἡ τοιαύτη πλάνη· ἀλλὰ τὸν Κύριον τῆς κτίσεως σαρκωθέντα τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγον προσκυνοῦμεν. Εἰ γὰρ καὶ ἡ σὰρξ αὐτὴ καθ' ἑαυτὴν μέρος ἐστὶ τῶν κτισμάτων, ἀλλὰ Θεοῦ γέγονε σῶμα. Καὶ οὔτε τὸ τοιοῦτον σῶμα καθ' ἑαυτὸ διαι ροῦντες ἀπὸ τοῦ Λόγου προσκυνοῦμεν· οὔτε τὸν Λόγον προσκυνῆσαι θέλοντες, μακρύνομεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς σαρκός· ἀλλ' εἰδότες, καθὰ προείπομεν, τὸ, Ὁ Λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο, τοῦτον καὶ ἐν σαρκὶ γενόμε νον, ἐπιγινώσκομεν Θεόν. Τίς τοιγαροῦν οὕτως ἄφρων ἐστὶν, ὡς λέγειν τῷ Κυρίῳ· Ἀπόστα ἀπὸ τοῦ σώματος, ἵνα σε προσκυνήσω; Ἢ τίς οὕτως ἀσεβής ἐστιν, ὡς μετὰ τῶν ἀφρόνων Ἰουδαίων διὰ τὸ σῶμα λέγειν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί σὺ, ἄνθρωπος ὢν, ποιεῖς σεαυτὸν Θεόν; Ἀλλ' οὐ τοιοῦτος ὁ λεπρός· προσεκύνει γὰρ τὸν Θεὸν ἐν σώματι ὄντα, καὶ ἐγίνωσκεν, ὅτι Θεὸς ἦν, λέγων· Κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς, δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι. Καὶ οὔτε διὰ τὴν σάρκα ἐνόμισε κτίσμα τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγον· οὔτε διὰ τὸ εἶναι τὸν Λόγον δημιουργὸν πάσης κτίσεως, ἐξουθένει τὴν σάρκα, ἣν ἐνδεδυμένος ἦν· ἀλλ' ὡς ἐν κτιστῷ ναῷ τὸν κτίστην τοῦ παντὸς προσεκύνει, καὶ ἐκαθαρίζετο. Οὕτως καὶ ἡ αἱμοῤῥοοῦσα γυνὴ, πιστεύσασα καὶ μόνον ἁψαμένη τοῦ κρασπέδου, ἰάθη· καὶ ἡ μὲν θάλαττα ἐπαφρίζουσα τοῖς κύμασιν ἤκουσε τοῦ σαρκωθέντος Λόγου, καὶ πέπαυται τοῦ χειμῶνος· ὁ δὲ ἐκ γενετῆς τυφλὸς, πτύσματι τῆς σαρκὸς τεθεράπευται παρὰ τοῦ Λόγου. Καὶ τό γε μεῖζον καὶ παραδοξότερον (ἴσως γὰρ τοῦτο καὶ τοὺς ἀσεβεστάτους ἐσκανδάλισε), καὶ ἐπ' αὐτοῦ τοῦ σταυροῦ κρεμαμένου τοῦ Κυρίου (αὐτοῦ γὰρ ἦν τὸ σῶμα, καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ ἦν ὁ Λόγος), ὁ μὲν ἥλιος ἐσκοτίσθη, ἡ δὲ γῆ ἐτρόμασεν, αἱ πέτραι ἐσχίσθησαν, καὶ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη, καὶ πολλὰ σώματα τῶν κεκοιμημένων ἁγίων ἀνέστη. Ταῦτα δὲ γέγονε, καὶ οὐδεὶς, ὥσπερ νῦν οἱ Ἀρειανοὶ τολμῶσι, διελογίσατο, εἰ δεῖ σαρκωθέντι τῷ Λόγῳ πείθεσθαι· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄνθρωπον βλέποντες, ἐπεγίνωσκον αὐτὸν ὄντα δημιουργὸν αὐτῶν· καὶ ἀνθρωπίνης φωνῆς ἀκούοντες, οὐ διὰ τὸ ἀνθρώπινον ἔλεγον, ὅτι ὁ Λόγος κτίσμα ἐστίν· ἀλλὰ καὶ μᾶλλον ἔτρεμον, καὶ οὐδὲν ἧττον ἐγίνωσκον, ἢ ὅτι ἐκ ναοῦ ἁγίου ἐφθέγγετο. Πῶς τοίνυν οἱ ἀσεβεῖς οὐ φοβοῦνται μὴ, καθὼς οὐκ ἐδοκίμασαν τὸν Θεὸν ἔχειν ἐν ἐπιγνώσει, παραδοθῶσιν εἰς ἀδόκιμον νοῦν, ποιεῖν τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα; Οὐ γὰρ κτίσματι ἡ κτίσις προσκυνεῖ· οὐδὲ πάλιν διὰ τὴν σάρκα παρῃτεῖτο τὸν Κύ ριον ἑαυτῆς προσκυνεῖν, ἀλλὰ τὸν ἑαυτῆς δημιουργὸν ἔβλεπεν ἐν σώματι· καὶ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πᾶν γόνυ ἔκαμπτε, καὶ κάμψει δὲ, ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων, καὶ καταχθονίων, καὶ πᾶσα γλῶσσα ἐξομολογήσεται, κἂν τοῖς Ἀρειανοῖς μὴ δοκῇ, ὅτι Κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς εἰς δόξαν Θεοῦ Πατρός. Οὐ γὰρ ἀδοξίαν ἤνεγκεν ἡ σὰρξ τῷ Λόγῳ· μὴ γένοιτο! ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον αὕτη δεδόξασται παρ' αὐτοῦ. Οὐδὲ, ἐπειδὴ δούλου μορφὴν ἀνέλαβεν ὁ ἐν μορφῇ Θεοῦ ὑπάρχων Υἱὸς, ἠλαττώθη τῆς θεότητος· ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον αὐτὸς ἐλευθερωτὴς πάσης σαρκὸς καὶ πάσης κτίσεως γέγονε.
thought_title: Worshiping the Creator in the flesh
orientation: Athanasius is answering the Arians' charge that Christians worship a creature, and he now states the Church's true worship of the Word who became flesh.
pass_a_gloss: We do not worship a creature; may it never be! For of pagans and of Arians is such error; but we worship the Lord of creation, the Word of God, who became flesh. For even if the flesh itself by itself is a part of the creatures, yet it has become God's body. And neither do we, dividing such a body by itself from the Word, worship it; nor, wishing to worship the Word, do we distance him from the flesh; but knowing, as we said before, the saying, The Word became flesh, we recognize this one also as God when he has come to be in flesh. Who therefore is so foolish as to say to the Lord: Depart from the body, so that I may worship you? Or who is so impious as, with the foolish Jews, because of the body to say to him: Why do you, being a man, make yourself God? But the leper was not such; for he worshiped God being in a body, and he knew that he was God, saying: Lord, if you wish, you are able to cleanse me. And neither because of the flesh did he consider the Word of God a creature; nor because the Word is maker of all creation did he despise the flesh which he had put on; but as in a created temple he worshiped the Creator of all, and he was cleansed. So also the woman with the flow of blood, having believed and only touched the fringe, was healed; and the sea, foaming with waves, heard the Word who had become flesh, and it ceased from the storm; and the man blind from birth was healed by the spittle of the flesh by the Word. And what is greater and more paradoxical (for perhaps this also scandalized the most impious), even while the Lord himself was hanging on the cross (for his was the body, and in it was the Word), the sun was darkened, and the earth trembled, the rocks were split, and the curtain of the temple was torn, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep arose. And these things happened, and no one, as now the Arians dare, reasoned whether one must obey the Word who has become flesh; but even seeing a man, they recognized him as being their maker; and hearing a human voice, they did not say because of the human element that the Word is a creature; but rather they trembled, and they knew no less than that he was speaking from a holy temple. How then do the impious not fear lest, just as they did not see fit to have God in knowledge, they be handed over to a worthless mind, to do what is not fitting? For creation does not worship a creature; nor again because of the flesh did it refuse to worship its own Lord, but it saw its own maker in a body; and at the name of Jesus Christ every knee bent, and will bend, of heavenly and earthly and subterranean beings, and every tongue will confess, even if it does not seem good to the Arians, that Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father. For the flesh did not bring dishonor to the Word; may it never be! but rather it has been glorified by him. Nor, since the Son who exists in the form of God took the form of a slave, was he diminished in divinity; but rather he himself became liberator of all flesh and of all creation.

choices.english: We do not worship a creature
choices.why: Keeps the fronted negation and the glossary term 'creature' for κτίσμα; the verb 'worship' is the glossary rendering for προσκυνεῖν.
rejected: It is not a creature we worship

choices.term: τὸν Κύριον τῆς κτίσεως σαρκωθέντα τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγον
choices.english: the Lord of creation, the Word of God, who became flesh
choices.why: Preserves the appositional structure and the glossary terms 'the Word' and 'flesh'; 'Lord of creation' keeps κτίσις distinct from κτίσμα.
rejected: the incarnate Lord of creation, the Word of God
the Lord of the creation made flesh, the Word of God

choices.why: Literal rendering of the perfect tense and the genitive of possession; 'body' is the natural English for σῶμα in this context.
rejected: it became the body of God
it has come to be a body of God

choices.term: ἐν κτιστῷ ναῷ τὸν κτίστην τοῦ παντὸς προσεκύνει
choices.english: as in a created temple he worshiped the Creator of all
choices.why: Keeps the contrast between κτιστός and κτίστης, and uses the glossary terms 'temple' and 'Creator'; 'as in' renders the ὡς of manner.
rejected: in a created shrine he worshiped the Maker of all
he worshiped the Creator of all in a created temple

choices.term: ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πᾶν γόνυ ἔκαμπτε, καὶ κάμψει δέ
choices.english: at the name of Jesus Christ every knee bent, and will bend
choices.why: Keeps the imperfect and future tenses of the verb, and the Pauline allusion is rendered literally without smoothing the tense shift.
rejected: at the name of Jesus Christ every knee bows and will bow
every knee bent and will bend at the name of Jesus Christ

choices.term: ἐλευθερωτὴς πάσης σαρκὸς καὶ πάσης κτίσεως
choices.english: liberator of all flesh and of all creation
choices.why: Literal rendering of ἐλευθερωτής as 'liberator' and κτίσις as 'creation', distinct from κτίσμα ('creature').
rejected: redeemer of all flesh and all creation
freer of all flesh and all creation

pass_b_english: We do not worship a creature. Never! That is the error of pagans and Arians. We worship the Lord of creation, the Word of God, who became flesh. For even if the flesh in itself is part of created things, it has become God's body. And we do not worship such a body by dividing it from the Word and taking it on its own, nor, when we want to worship the Word, do we push him far away from the flesh. Rather, knowing, as we said before, that "the Word became flesh" (John 1:14), we recognize him as God even when he has come in the flesh. Who, then, is so foolish as to say to the Lord, "Leave your body so that I may worship you"? Or who is so impious as to say to him, along with the foolish Jews, because of the body, "Why do you, being a man, make yourself God?" (John 10:33; cf. John 8:40). But the leper was not like that. He worshiped God who was present in a body, and he knew that he was God, saying, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean" (Matthew 8:2). He did not think the Word of God was a creature because of the flesh, nor did he despise the flesh the Word had put on because the Word is the maker of every creature. Rather, as in a created temple he worshiped the Creator of all, and he was made clean. So too the woman with the flow of blood believed, and merely touching the fringe of his garment, she was healed. The sea, foaming with waves, heard the Word who had become flesh, and the storm ceased. The man blind from birth was healed by the Word through the spittle of the flesh. And what is greater and more astonishing—for perhaps this is what scandalized even the most impious—while the Lord himself hung on the cross (for the body was his, and the Word was in it), the sun was darkened, the earth shook, the rocks were split, the curtain of the temple was torn, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised (Matthew 27:51-52). These things happened, and no one reasoned, as the Arians now dare to do, about whether one should obey the Word who had become flesh. Even seeing a man, they recognized him as their maker. Even hearing a human voice, they did not say, because of his humanity, that the Word is a creature. Rather, they trembled all the more, and they knew no less that he was speaking from a holy temple. How then are the impious not afraid that, just as they did not see fit to acknowledge God, they may be handed over to a debased mind to do what ought not to be done (Romans 1:28)? For creation does not worship a creature, nor again did it refuse to worship its Lord because of the flesh. It saw its own maker in a body, and at the name of Jesus Christ every knee bent, and will bend, in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and every tongue will confess, even if the Arians do not think so, that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father (Philippians 2:10-11). For the flesh did not bring dishonor to the Word. Never! Rather, it has been glorified by him. Nor, because the Son who was in the form of God took the form of a servant, was he diminished in his divinity (Philippians 2:6-7). Rather, he himself became the liberator of all flesh and of all creation.

problems.source_quote: εἰ δεῖ σαρκωθέντι τῷ Λόγῳ πείθεσθαι
problems.why: πείθεσθαι means 'obey,' not 'trust'; the question is about obeying the incarnate Word.
problems.fix: about whether one should obey the Word who had become flesh
problems.ruling: πείθεσθαι means 'obey,' not 'trust'; meaning shifted from obedience to faith.

edits.old: about whether one should trust the Word who had become flesh
edits.new: about whether one should obey the Word who had become flesh

fixed: Changed 'trust' to 'obey' because πείθεσθαι means 'obey,' not 'trust'; the source asks whether one must obey the incarnate Word.

problems.why: τὸ ἀνθρώπινον refers to the human voice/person, not abstract 'human element'.

fixed: Changed 'because of the human element' to 'because of his humanity' to match διὰ τὸ ἀνθρώπινον, which refers to the human voice/person, not an abstract element.

problems.source_quote: Διὰ τί σὺ, ἄνθρωπος ὢν, ποιεῖς σεαυτὸν Θεόν;
problems.why: John 10:33 has Jews saying 'you make yourself God' but not 'being a man'; John 5:18 or John 8:40/8:58 contexts differ. The closest match is John 10:33 for the charge, but 'being a man' (ἄνθρωπος ὢν) appears in John 8:40 and John 5:18 has different wording. However, the exact phrase 'being a man' with 'make yourself God' is not in John 10:33. The citation is imprecise; the verse reference does not fully match the words quoted.

fixed: The citation (John 10:33) is imprecise because the quoted words 'being a man' (ἄνθρωπος ὢν) do not appear in John 10:33; the closest match for that phrase is John 8:40, so I added a cross-reference.

last_rejected.quote: Rather, they trembled all the more, and they knew no less that he was speaking from a holy temple.
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλὰ καὶ μᾶλλον ἔτρεμον, καὶ οὐδὲν ἧττον ἐγίνωσκον, ἢ ὅτι ἐκ ναοῦ ἁγίου ἐφθέγγετο.
last_rejected.why: Source says 'they knew no less THAN THAT he was speaking from a holy temple'; English drops the comparative 'than that' (ἢ ὅτι), losing the claim's force.
last_rejected.fix: Rather, they trembled all the more, and they knew no less than that he was speaking from a holy temple.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'knew no less that' captures ἢ ὅτι adequately; comparative force is implicit in 'no less'

last_rejected.quote: He did not think the Word of God was a creature because of the flesh, nor did he despise the flesh the Word had put on because the Word is the maker of every creature.
last_rejected.source_quote: Καὶ οὔτε διὰ τὴν σάρκα ἐνόμισε κτίσμα τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγον· οὔτε διὰ τὸ εἶναι τὸν Λόγον δημιουργὸν πάσης κτίσεως, ἐξουθένει τὴν σάρκα, ἣν ἐνδεδυμένος ἦν
last_rejected.why: English 'nor did he despise' makes both clauses about the leper, but Greek οὔτε...οὔτε coordinates two distinct subjects: the leper did not think the Word a creature, and (by implication) the Word did not despise the flesh. The second clause's subject is the Word, not the leper.
last_rejected.fix: He did not think the Word of God a creature because of the flesh, nor, because the Word is maker of every creature, did he despise the flesh he had put on.
last_rejected.ruling: οὔτε...οὔτε coordinates two actions of the leper; ἐξουθένει is singular and contextually the leper didn't despise the flesh.

last_rejected.quote: they may be handed over to a debased mind to do what ought not to be done
last_rejected.source_quote: παραδοθῶσιν εἰς ἀδόκιμον νοῦν, ποιεῖν τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα
last_rejected.why: Greek ποιεῖν is infinitive of purpose/result, not 'to do what ought not to be done' (which suggests moral duty). The sense is 'to do things that are unfitting/inappropriate'—the debased mind produces improper actions.
last_rejected.fix: handed over to a debased mind, to do what is unfitting
last_rejected.ruling: τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα means 'things not proper/fitting'; 'ought not to be done' is standard rendering of καθήκοντα, not a major error.
